page.title: Overview
page.purpose: Show how local scenarios become publicly reachable, which routes are trustworthy, and what the operator should do next.

priorities.statement: The exposure boundary is understandable at a glance.
priorities.notes: The hero visualization should show the tunnel, exposed scenarios, route health, lease state, and the protected-versus-public asset boundary.

priorities.statement: The next operator action is explicit.
priorities.notes: Missing credentials, port violations, failed probes, and expiring leases must become actionable findings, not passive badges.
Counts and any health score must link to the routes and checks that produced them.

states.description: Tunnel, exposure, readiness, and recovery data are loading.
The exposure constellation and operator findings are visible.
Some domain data is unavailable while the remaining route picture stays visible and names the missing source.
The last complete picture remains visible while refresh is pending.
Local operation is available, but remote Cloudflare reconciliation is blocked by missing credentials.
No routes are exposed; the page explains that local scenarios remain private and offers the first exposure action.
The page names which operational read failed and provides retry.

claims.statement: The exposure topology is a meaningful operational projection: every scenario node and connection corresponds to route, probe, lease, or policy state.
Every non-healthy finding names its cause, scope, and next operator action.
When remote operation is unavailable, the missing credential and the blocked capability are visible without navigating away from the overview.
